html:
The Burmese nationalist who founded the modern army of Burma and negotiated its independence from Britain, then was assassinated six months before it came.

As a student leader at Rangoon University in the 1930s he joined the Thakin movement against British rule. In 1940 he left for Japan and became one of the "Thirty Comrades" trained by the Japanese. They returned with the Japanese invasion in 1942 at the head of the Burma Independence Army.

Japanese rule soon proved harsh. In March 1945 Aung San turned his army against Japan and joined the Allies. After the war he led the push for independence. In January 1947 he signed an agreement with British prime minister Clement Attlee in London, and in February he made the Panglong Agreement with leaders of the Shan, Kachin and Chin peoples.

On 19 July 1947 gunmen sent by a rival politician killed him and six cabinet colleagues. Burma became independent in January 1948 without him. He is honoured as the father of the nation, and his daughter Aung San Suu Kyi took up his name in politics.
sum: The Burmese nationalist who founded the modern army of Burma and negotiated its independence from Britain, then was assassinated six months before it came.
